rationale: Round 0 built and ran correctly, so this round raises obfuscation pressure while respecting the program's profile: evalloop is a tiny (800-byte, 4-function) interpreter-style benchmark whose hot path is an eval loop with an indirect dispatch (execute is a 7-byte trampoline, pointing at indirect calls), making the indirection passes (ICALL, IGV) and branch/opaque restructuring (IBR, FLA, BCF) the highest-value transforms for hiding the dispatch structure and static call graph; their RuntimeCost weights are held around 0.3-0.6 because the hot loop is loop-dominated rather than straight-line FP arithmetic, so flattening and bogus control flow cost less here than in the flops/fbench-style kernels that merely share the source tree, and the tiny text size means SizeCost can stay permissive (0.5-0.7). SUB stays a cheap baseline transform with elevated DiversityGain for arithmetic scrambling of the interpreter's opcode handling, SPLIT is kept moderate since it mainly amplifies the other passes on the already-small eval/main bodies, and CorrectnessRisk is kept high (0.9+) across all passes because round 0 demonstrated clean semantics and we want to preserve that while trading for more SecurityGain/DiversityGain; no pass is disabled since the program's small size and demonstrated build headroom tolerate full-stack application.
